title: Retail drug business limb: patients, extension, vaccines and dosage modification, disease-state reference, referral, notice and consent
rule_summary: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2(c)(5) allows collaborative drug therapy management by a collaborating pharmacist in a retail drug business, as registered in section 38 of chapter 112 and limited by this section, with supervision by a physician according to the terms of his collaborative practice agreement and limited to the following: patients 18 years of age or older; an extension by 30 days of current drug therapy prescribed by the supervising physician; and administration of vaccines or the modification of dosages of medications prescribed by the supervising physician for asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, congestive heart failure, HIV or AIDS, osteoporosis and co-morbidities identified by the supervising physician for the individual patient along with the primary diagnosis. The collaborative practice agreement shall specifically reference each disease state being co-managed. A patient shall be referred by a supervising physician to that physician's collaborating pharmacist and shall be given notice of the collaboration and shall consent to the collaboration. The clause was inserted by St. 2008, c. 528, s. 3, approved January 15, 2009, and the current text of clause (5) reads as enacted.
exam_relevance: Tests the closed list of what a retail collaborative practice agreement may reach: patients 18 or older, a 30-day extension of the supervising physician's current therapy, and vaccine administration or dosage modification for the named diseases and physician-identified co-morbidities, together with the disease-state reference, referral, notice and consent sentences.

authority.name: Acts of 2008, Chapter 528 (An Act establishing collaborative drug therapy management)

numeric_facts.fact: Minimum patient age in the retail drug business setting
Extension of current drug therapy prescribed by the supervising physician

common_confusions: The words limited to the following make the clause's list a ceiling on what a retail agreement may reach.
The extension is of current drug therapy prescribed by the supervising physician; the clause does not describe it as a power to start a different therapy.
A disease state that appears in the statutory list is not thereby co-managed for a patient; the agreement shall specifically reference each disease state being co-managed.
The referral runs from a supervising physician to that physician's collaborating pharmacist, and notice and consent are stated as two requirements.
verification_notes: Read in the current text of M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2 on malegislature.gov on 2026-09-17, and compared with the text inserted by St. 2008, c. 528, s. 3 as published on malegislature.gov the same day. The session law contains three sections, no separate effective-date section, and is marked approved January 15, 2009.
